title: Stationary point and the value of a derivative at a limit
statement:
The curve
$$y = x^3 - 3x + k$$
has two distinct turning points.

Find the values of $x$ at these turning points, and determine the values of $k$ for which the curve touches the $x$-axis.
solution:
Differentiate:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 3 = 3(x^2 - 1) = 3(x-1)(x+1).$$

Setting $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$ gives turning points at $x = -1$ and $x = 1$.

The corresponding $y$-values are:
$$y(-1) = (-1)^3 - 3(-1) + k = -1 + 3 + k = k + 2,$$
$$y(1) = 1 - 3 + k = k - 2.$$

The curve touches the $x$-axis exactly when one of these turning points lies on the $x$-axis, i.e. when $y = 0$ at a turning point.

Therefore either
$$k + 2 = 0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad k = -2,$$
or
$$k - 2 = 0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad k = 2.$$

Hence the curve touches the $x$-axis when
$$\boxed{\,k = \pm 2\,}.$$

(At $k=2$ the turning point at $x=1$ touches the axis; at $k=-2$ the turning point at $x=-1$ touches the axis.)
hints: Differentiate and solve f'(x)=0 for the turning points.
Substitute each turning point x-value back into y.
The curve touches the x-axis when a turning point has y = 0.
